items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The new guard `if not ... is_cached(rel_obj) and not instance.get_deferred_fields():` appears in three places with no comment explaining why the deferred-fields check is there. Its purpose isn't obvious, and the long lines read less easily than the code around them.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The same compound guard is copied into ForwardManyToOneDescriptor, ReverseOneToOneDescriptor and the reverse-FK manager. The `get_deferred_fields()` part ties prefetch caching to deferred loading, which the conventions say not to do. The two-line is_cached guard was all that was needed.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Nothing is swallowed, but `not instance.get_deferred_fields()` stops back-references being cached whenever the parent uses only()/defer(). For example, User.objects.only('email').prefetch_related('profile') now runs an extra query on profile.user. The check also runs once per child row.

items.name: Guard is conditional and covers the one-to-one variant
items.name_zh: 仅在已缓存时跳过回填，并考虑一对一情形
items.evidence: The is_cached guard is there and the one-to-one path is covered. But the guard also relies on a deferred-field hack (`and not instance.get_deferred_fields()`), so prefetches without nesting no longer fill the reverse relation when the parent has deferred fields. The rubric marks deferred-field-based guards as bad.
